chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad narrated from Ali ibn al-Hasan, from al-Husayn ibn Rashid, from al-Murtajil ibn Ma'mar, from Dharih al-Muharibi, from Ubadah al-Asadi, from Habbat al-Urini, who said:

I went out with the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) to the back (of Kufa), so he paused at the Valley of Peace as if addressing a group of people. So I stood due to his standing until I was exhausted. Then I sat until I was tired. Then I stood until there came to me the likes of what came to me the first time. Then I sat down until I was tired. Then I stood and gathered my robe and I said, 'O Commander of the Faithful! I sympathize with you from the long standing, so rest for a while.' Then I spread the robe in order for him to sit upon it. So he said to me, 'O Habbat! It was only a discussion with a Believer, or comforting him.' I said, 'O Commander of the Faithful! And they are like that?' He said, 'Yes, and if the covering is uncovered for you, you would see them in groups and groups discussing.' So I said, 'Bodily or in spirit form?' So he said, 'The souls. There is none from a Believer who dies in a spot from the spots of the earth, except that it is said to his soul: 'Join at the valley of peace, and it is a spot from the Garden of Eden'.

key_terms.وَادِي السَّلَامِ: Valley of Peace (a famous graveyard in Kufa)

ai.seo_question: What happens to the souls of believers after death according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Kafi, Imam Ali (peace be upon him) reveals to Habba al-Uranni that his prolonged standing in Wadi al-Salam was not physical fatigue but spiritual communion with the gathered souls of the faithful. This hadith is pivotal in Shia theology for establishing the reality of the soul's continued existence and social interaction in the Barzakh, specifically identifying Wadi al-Salam as a blessed enclave within Paradise where believers converse in their spiritual forms.
